chapters.title: My parents, and reinterpreting the past

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Because — do you assume that all relationships are unhappy? I'll tell you why I did. Because I've done years of therapy. Growing up, I saw a lot of unhappy relationships. What I interpreted — now, if my parents are watching, God, I hope they're not — it's not about them, it's about me. What did I see? I saw, in lots of places, people fighting, I saw yelling. And I was terrified of it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I remember clearly the decision I made one day. I was like five years old. I was watching a party. My family was Ukrainian and Irish, on that side of the family. And they like to party — I mean, they could drink. That's water, by the way. But they pounded the drinks. So I'm four or five years old, sitting at the top of the stairs — and from the top of the stairs in my grandmother's house, you could see the whole living room. There were cousins and aunts and uncles — it's a huge family. That generation had like nine kids each. The point is, there were lots and lots of people. And I just remember watching what I was observing, of the way people were treating each other. What I observed as a four- or five-year-old — I don't really know what was going on, and it doesn't matter. Obviously, the older I got, the more I realized that maybe I was misinterpreting it. But I decided, in that moment: if all relationships are like this, then I don't want one. I'd rather be alone.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So how did that work out for me? Anytime there was any kind of fight or disagreement in a relationship, that equaled failure to me. Relationship over. Ciao, bye. How did that work out for me? You see? Because of some decision I made when I was four years old.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Then you can ask even more questions. Why did I have the seed to see it that way? Where did that seed come from? Where did that cause come from? You can start exploring the why. But then, when you do that kind of exercise, you're like — what was I misinterpreting? I was the dog. I was seeing failed relationships. And then you look back and you're like — really? I mean, how you define a relationship is different, but there were no divorces in my family, ever. They lasted forever. And then I'm like — were they treating each other badly, or were they just having fun? Well, mom and dad did a pretty good job. And then you start rejoicing that I had a mom and dad that were together, and that they worked through whatever challenges they had — and they were able to. Sometimes you can't work through that, and that makes sense too. I'm not judging whether someone should stay together or not — that's not what I'm saying. But I'm like, wow, that's quite fortunate. I didn't have to struggle in a different way.

chapters.title: Four powers at the same time

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now guess what I'm doing? What am I tartuking about? And then I asked the question: why did I have that coolness happening in my life? Where did that seed come from? Wow, that's freaking awesome. What did I do to create a family that had some kind of stability? Did we have problems? Yes. Did I spend years on the couch? Yes. We all have our things.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But the thing is, when you turn your mind to the good things in the middle of the negativities — now you're doing what we did last night. We're doing four powers at the same time. And you're immediately replanting different kinds of seeds. Does it mean the bad things didn't happen? They did. Did it hurt? God, it did. And I'm sorry if you had to go through anything like that. I can imagine some of those things, and I wish they didn't happen. But we're here now, today. So what are we going to do with that? Are we going to carry it with us and then pull it up when we're 90 years old and about to fall into the ground, and gravity just takes over and we die? Let's do it now. I want to be happy now. I don't want to wait to be happy then — and by that point, I'll probably regret that I didn't do it when I was younger.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So make a commitment to look at yourself. We're going to go through some topics. I'm going to list a few potential limiting beliefs we might have. You might resonate with it, maybe you don't at all. But after we do each group, I'm going to give you a few minutes to think about what some of your own beliefs about that are.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So we're going to talk about the thing that everybody wants. Money. Here's a couple of ideas — I can't even see this.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Money is the source of all evil.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Having too much money is a bad thing.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I need to have money saved because something bad might happen.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm only able to make enough to sustain my life.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: It's impossible to have extra.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: You only live once, so spend it all today.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: You only live once, so sacrifice today for a better tomorrow.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Money is hard to get.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm just not good at managing money.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: If I think about money, I can't be spiritual.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: If I want more money, I'm greedy.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: If I have a lot of money, people will judge me negatively.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now take a few moments and think about your own relationship with money.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Did any of those resonate with you? Or are there other ones that popped in there, like, well, actually, this is my thing? And then the fact that that drink spilled and people couldn't pay attention — maybe they weren't able to think about those questions because it's too difficult. I'm just suggesting; I'm not saying. But sometimes we get distracted, even with kindness, to avoid the part that really shakes our core. It's still a good seed. Remember what I said yesterday about being creative so I didn't have to speak Spanish? It's a mixed seed.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So think about money. Take another minute. What do you think about money, and your relationship to it? Is it impossible? Is it a challenge? Is it easy for you? If you don't have enough, or you want more, there's probably something you think — either about it or about yourself.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: All right, one minute.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Okay, we're going to move on to the next topic. Relationships — romantic relationships.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I have one idea about what a relationship is, and I want nothing other than that.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I will only settle for a partner who is perfect.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: My relationships don't work because there's something wrong with me.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I don't want a relationship because of the negative relationships I saw growing up.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Relationships take too much work.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Relationships are always hard.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm doomed to have a bad relationship forever.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: My partner can never truly understand me.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm afraid to tell my partner who I really am.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm afraid my partner won't love me if they know who I truly am.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: It's going to get intense. Take a minute to add any of your own that might come up.
